jobs.description:
Our Story

Our small Canadian-born business was founded in 1978 and has become a global organization that now spans 120 locations across 20 countries. Our expansion has been rapid, but what matters most is the common belief that drives all 5,000 of our people to be a different type of real estate organization. We believe that the places in which we live, work and play have the power to make us happier and healthier, and we are united by a shared sense of purpose, to have a positive impact on people’s lives. In short, we are a global commercial real estate advisory firm with a simple aim for real estate to play a leading role in creating vibrant buildings, cities and places that deliver long-lasting social value and economic impact.

Why Work for Us

We believe that our industry is changing, and we want our business to be a melting pot of curious minds, passionate hearts and strategic intelligence. Your gender, religion and race are all highly respected, but are less important to us than your ability to step up and change the game. We provide you with a place where you can do just that, with like-minded people. Collaboration is embedded in the way we work - our people have the autonomy to collaborate on client relationships, engage teams across the business, lead operations, work collectively on projects, participate in strategy and are ultimately responsible for our growth. Our distinctive Principal-led, privately-owned model puts us in the enviable position of being able to offer every employee the opportunity to own a share of our business and inspires and allows anyone to become a Principal. This role carries voting rights, so our people have a very real say in the future direction and operation of our business. This means that we are able to attract, engage and retain the best talent from the industry.

Build more than just your career

As a graduate in our London planning consultancy team, you will be supported through your journey towards becoming a Chartered Planner with the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI). You will have the opportunity to work on a range of challenging projects, providing high quality planning advice to private and public sector clients. At the same time, we’ll support you in completing your assessment of professional competence (APC).

Real opportunities, real responsibility

You’ll join us on a journey to become a professionally qualified planner with membership of The Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI). Not only will you be working alongside industry leading professionals, you will be allocated a dedicated mentor to assist you during your training as well as RTPI focused APC workshops. We also run a global mentoring programme which graduates are actively encouraged to join and take advantage of.

You will work within a collaborative and supportive team, helping our clients to achieve their property and development related objectives through the provision of accurate and robust advice and effective, efficient, and timely engagement in the planning system. You will provide support to more senior members of the team on major, complex projects as well as advising and supporting other parts of the business where required.

We value graduates who aren’t afraid to step up and change the game. With that in mind, we’re looking for

A team player who is also able to lead with humility
A University Degree/Masters in a fully accredited RTPI course
An ability to challenge for the better
A strong drive for results, with an unwavering focus on the end game
The desire to adapt to anything, and demonstrate agility when things don’t go to plan
A passion for building great relationships with external and internal clients
An ability to look ahead, and to understand the commercial landscape
A talent for inspiring and energising those around you

At Avison Young, we’ve always put people at the heart of what we do.

In the last few years, we’ve increased the diversity at our board, leadership and Principal levels. Avison Young stands out for our commitment to empowering women. In addition to increasing the number of women on our board and in our leadership ranks, our internal Women’s Network of more than 500 members come together for networking and learning, and advise the business on strategies for promoting access, opportunity and inclusion in our industry.

Our global DEI steering committee shapes our strategy to continue to increase industry access for underrepresented groups and accelerating initiatives led by our employee resource groups, including our Women’s Network, Black Professionals and LGBTQ+ groups. In addition to leading global initiatives, the steering committee’s work examines our policies and practices, creating accountability for results and communicating progress to our executive leadership, our clients and our communities.

Our culture is underpinned by our approach to diversity, inclusion, and well-being. We are committed to building an inclusive culture that

empowers all our employees to thrive,
reflects all backgrounds and talents,
allows individuals to be successful and feel a sense of belonging,
and foster a workplace that is supported, inclusive and has a strong sense of community between colleagues.

Avison Young is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to treating all its employees and job applicants equitably. This includes implementing deliberate strategies that advance underrepresented communities in commercial real estate careers.

As a Disability Confident Employer, we are committed to removing any obstacles to inclusion. If you need any adjustments to support your application or any part of the recruitment process, such as information in alternative formats or special requirements to access our buildings, or you are eligible under the Disability Confident Scheme please contact us at careers.uk@avisonyoung.com<mailtocareers.uk@avisonyoung.com> and we will do everything we can to help.

We are committed to inclusion in our hiring processes, and we want to give everyone a chance to show what they can bring to our organisation. If you are not sure that you have all the skills in the person specification, please still apply. We value passion and potential in our employees, so it would be great to hear from you and why you would suit this position.

Some of our roles may be remote and some roles may be specific to our offices, but you will need to confirm you have the right to work in the UK.

Job Description

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role in Ramboll’s Town Planning team could be the perfect opportunity.

Your new role

You will bring your knowledge of Town Planning into play as you take a lead role in advising on planning strategy, delivering planning applications, and providing day to day planning advice. You will have the opportunity to drive sustainable change through all stages in the project lifecycle across within development and infrastructure projects.

To succeed in this role, you will be able to apply an excellent understanding of Town Planning in the UK, in all stages of the project lifecycle from early-stage feasibility/risk appraisal, through to delivery of planning conditions, obligations and scheme revision.

You will also need the skills to disseminate changes in the planning system across Ramboll, to Clients and the team in which you will work and help lead; and be able to form and hold good Client relationships.

Your key responsibilities will be to:

Work with Directors to take a lead role in advising on planning strategy and project managing applications and appeals,
Lead others in such work and provide constructive feedback, being a core part of Ramboll’s Town Planning team and be recognised as key person within the team,
Contributing to business development activities, including the preparation of fee proposals, tender submissions, marketing materials and presentations but most importantly, be willing to maintain Client relationships
Support the team’s leadership and wider management with team functions, including mentoring junior members of the team.
Develop relationships, build networks and collaborate with Ramboll technical specialists.
Represent Ramboll at meetings with clients and at networking events.

Your new team

You will be part of our wider Development team, albeit working on both development and infrastructure projects. This is part our Global Impact Assessment Service Line which been especially successful in driving further growth, targeting large, strategic projects – though not exclusively. Our projects are wide ranging and diverse and include housing, mixed use, regeneration, energy, highways and data centres.

More widely, our UK business employs experts 19 locations and covers a breadth of consulting services structured around Town Planning and impact assessment, compliance, strategy and transactions, new initiatives and sustainability, product safety and stewardship, contaminated land, and Water. Ramboll’s clients include UK and global multinationals, utilities, local and central government and international institutions. Ramboll works flexibly and with this you will be part of an exciting team of experts, who respect each other and work towards a common goal.

About You

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. Whilst we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills, and capabilities that will set you up for success.

These include:

7 years+ of experience
A degree in Town Planning or a related degree and or Post Graduate qualifications in a relevant discipline
Professional Membership of the RTPI
Project delivery and Town Planning experience
Strong communication skills both written and oral, with the ability to liaise with colleagues and maintain good client relationships
A keenness for professional development and progression

What We Can Offer You

Commitment to your development
Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
Flexible work environment
27 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Matched pension contributions
Private medical cover and life assurance

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your CV and cover letter.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

Ramboll in the United Kingdom

Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a foundation-owned people company. Ramboll has a proven track record of sustainable and responsible business and is a top ten engineering and environmental and sustainability consultancy in the UK, with more than 1,500 employees across 16 offices working towards a more sustainable future. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Environment & Health, and Energy. Strong values guide what we do and drive an inclusive, collaborative, and highly flexible culture that values people and ideas. Explore and nurture your own passion, expertise, and creativity at Ramboll through work that benefits our people, partners, nature, and society.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. The Opportunity

Are you chartered town planner
looking to take the next step in your career by working on some of the UK's most exciting strategic planning, development and infrastructure projects?

We're looking for a Senior Planner or Associate Planner
to join our Planning team in Reading
. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a leading multidisciplinary consultancy, working on projects that shape communities, support sustainable growth and deliver lasting positive impact.

You'll work alongside experienced planners and technical specialists across transport, engineering, environmental services, architecture, landscape and sustainability, giving you the opportunity to broaden your expertise and play an increasingly influential role in the delivery of complex projects.

Our team works across a diverse portfolio, including strategic land, development management, residential, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure, regeneration and energy projects. You'll have the opportunity to develop your technical expertise, strengthen client relationships and take greater ownership of projects as your career progresses.

About The Role

As a Senior Planner or Associate Planner
, you'll play an important role in delivering planning projects for a diverse range of clients, while contributing to the continued growth and development of our Reading Planning team.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Managing and contributing to planning applications for a wide range of development projects.
Providing strategic planning and development management advice to clients.
Contributing to strategic planning and plan-making projects across the region and nationally.
Preparing planning appraisals, planning statements, reports and supporting documentation.
Preparing planning appeals including involvement in hearings and public inquires.
Undertaking policy research and monitoring changes in planning legislation and guidance.
Managing project programmes, budgets and delivery to agreed timescales.
Building and maintaining strong relationships with clients, local authorities and key stakeholders.
Working collaboratively with colleagues across multiple technical disciplines to deliver integrated solutions.
Supporting business development activities, including proposals and client presentations.
Identifying opportunities to support the growth of the Planning team and wider business.
For Associate Planner applicants, taking greater ownership of projects, leading client relationships and providing guidance and mentoring to more junior colleagues.
For Associate Planner applicants, supporting the development of the team through knowledge sharing, coaching and contributing to recruitment and wider team initiatives.

Your Impact

You'll contribute to projects that make a genuine difference to the places where people live, work and thrive.

Working across a variety of sectors, you'll help clients navigate complex planning challenges, secure planning permissions and deliver development that supports economic growth, creates new homes, improves infrastructure and enhances the environment.

You'll be part of a genuinely multidisciplinary environment, working alongside specialists across the business to develop integrated solutions and deliver better outcomes for communities and clients.

As your career develops, you'll be encouraged to take on greater responsibility, strengthen your client relationships and contribute to the continued growth and success of our Planning team.

About You

We're looking for experienced planners who are commercially aware, enjoy solving complex problems and are confident building relationships with clients and stakeholders.

You'll Have

A degree, and ideally a postgraduate qualification, in Town Planning or a related discipline.
MRTPI membership.
Significant experience within a planning consultancy, local authority, developer or related environment.
Strong knowledge of the UK planning system, including development management and/or plan making.
Experience preparing planning applications, appraisals, planning statements and technical reports.
Strong report writing, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
The ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work to agreed deadlines.
A collaborative approach and genuine interest in sustainable development.
For Senior Planner level, experience managing planning projects and developing client relationships.
For Associate Planner level, a track record of taking ownership of projects, managing client relationships and supporting or mentoring junior colleagues.

We're particularly interested in hearing from planners with experience across strategic land, residential, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure, regeneration or energy
, although relevant experience in other areas of planning will also be considered.

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. Named ‘Best Place to Work’ and ‘International Consulting Firm of the Year’ at the NCE Awards 2024.
